question: Which of the following is a source of light?
options: The Sun
The Moon
A glass mirror
A shiny metal spoon
answer: The Sun

question: How are we able to see a textbook placed on a wooden desk in a brightly lit classroom?
options: Light from the lamp reflects off the textbook into our eyes
The textbook produces its own light which enters our eyes
Our eyes shine light onto the textbook
Light travels directly from our eyes to the lamp
answer: Light from the lamp reflects off the textbook into our eyes

question: Why can we see the Moon at night even though it is not a source of light?
options: It reflects light from the Sun into our eyes
It produces its own light when the sky gets dark
It absorbs sunlight during the day and glows at night
Light from street lamps on Earth reflects off the Moon
answer: It reflects light from the Sun into our eyes

question: Siti enters a completely dark room with no light sources. Why is she unable to see a red apple on the table?
options: There is no light to reflect off the apple into her eyes
The apple stops reflecting red light in the dark
Human eyes cannot function without sunlight
The apple becomes transparent in total darkness
answer: There is no light to reflect off the apple into her eyes

question: Which object allows ALL or MOST light to pass through it?
options: Clear plastic sheet
Frosted glass window
Thick wooden block
Aluminium foil
answer: Clear plastic sheet

question: Ali tried to look at a lit candle through a bent plastic pipe. He could not see the flame. What property of light does this demonstrate?
options: Light travels in straight lines
Light can bend around curved objects
Light reflects off plastic pipes
Light cannot travel through air
answer: Light travels in straight lines

question: Why is a shadow formed when a wooden toy is placed in front of a turned-on torch?
options: The wooden toy blocks light because light travels in straight lines
The torch pulls darkness toward the wooden toy
The wooden toy absorbs all the heat from the torch
Light bends around the wooden toy and creates a dark area
answer: The wooden toy blocks light because light travels in straight lines

question: Three sheets of different materials (X, Y, and Z) were placed in front of a torch. Sheet X formed a dark shadow, Sheet Y formed a faint shadow, and Sheet Z formed no shadow. Which row correctly identifies the materials?
options: X: Cardboard, Y: Tracing paper, Z: Clear glass
X: Clear glass, Y: Cardboard, Z: Tracing paper
X: Tracing paper, Y: Clear glass, Z: Cardboard
X: Cardboard, Y: Clear glass, Z: Tracing paper
answer: X: Cardboard, Y: Tracing paper, Z: Clear glass

question: What type of shadow will a clear glass cup cast on a screen when light shines on it?
options: No shadow or a very faint shadow
A very dark shadow
A shadow shaped like a square
A shadow much larger than an opaque cup
answer: No shadow or a very faint shadow

question: John wants to make the shadow of a wooden ball on the screen LARGER. What should he do?
options: Move the wooden ball closer to the torch
Move the wooden ball further from the torch
Move the screen closer to the wooden ball
Move the torch further from the wooden ball
answer: Move the wooden ball closer to the torch

question: In an experiment, Meiling keeps the distance between the torch and the screen constant. What happens to the size of the shadow if she moves the object CLOSER to the screen?
options: The shadow becomes smaller
The shadow becomes larger
The shadow stays the same size
No shadow will be formed on the screen
answer: The shadow becomes smaller

question: Devi set up a torch, an opaque mug, and a screen. Which change will result in the SMALLEST shadow on the screen?
options: Torch furthest from mug, screen closest to mug
Torch closest to mug, screen furthest from mug
Torch closest to mug, screen closest to mug
Torch furthest from mug, screen furthest from mug
answer: Torch furthest from mug, screen closest to mug

question: To investigate how the distance between a torch and an object affects shadow size, which variable MUST be kept the same?
options: Distance between the object and the screen
Distance between the torch and the object
Size of the shadow on the screen
Position of the light source
answer: Distance between the object and the screen

question: A student moved a torch closer to an opaque cylinder and recorded the shadow height: at 40 cm away, shadow was 10 cm; at 30 cm away, shadow was 15 cm; at 20 cm away, shadow was 20 cm. What shadow height can be expected when the torch is 10 cm away?
options: 25 cm
15 cm
10 cm
5 cm
answer: 25 cm

question: A solid cone is placed between a torch and a screen. Depending on how the cone is positioned relative to the torch, which two shadow shapes can it form?
options: A circle and a triangle
A circle and a square
A triangle and a rectangle
An oval and a square
answer: A circle and a triangle

question: A cylindrical wooden block can form two different shadow shapes on a screen depending on how it is held. What are these two shapes?
options: A circle and a rectangle
A circle and a triangle
A square and a triangle
An oval and a square
answer: A circle and a rectangle

question: At what time of the day will a vertical flagpole outdoors cast its SHORTEST shadow on the ground?
options: 12:00 pm (noon)
8:00 am (morning)
5:00 pm (late afternoon)
7:00 pm (sunset)
answer: 12:00 pm (noon)

question: Why is a person's shadow on the ground longest in the early morning and late afternoon?
options: The Sun is low in the sky, shining at a sharp slant
The Sun is directly overhead
Light travels slower in the morning and evening
The Sun produces more light during these times
answer: The Sun is low in the sky, shining at a sharp slant

question: An opaque square card with a triangular hole cut out of its center is placed between a torch and a screen. What shadow will appear on the screen?
options: A dark square shadow with a bright triangular patch in the center
A dark triangular shadow with a bright square patch in the center
A completely dark square shadow with no bright patch
A completely bright screen with a dark triangle
answer: A dark square shadow with a bright triangular patch in the center

question: Ben shines a torch at a ball on a table from Position A (directly above), Position B (at 45 degrees), and Position C (low on the side). Which position produces the LONGEST shadow?
options: Position C
Position A
Position B
Positions A and C give equal shadows
answer: Position C

question: An experiment measured light passing through four material sheets (P, Q, R, S) using a light sensor. Light sensor readings: P = 0 units, Q = 450 units, R = 150 units, S = 900 units. The torch produced 900 units. Which sheet is OPAQUE?
options: Sheet P
Sheet Q
Sheet R
Sheet S
answer: Sheet P

question: Based on the experiment data above (Torch = 900 units; P = 0, Q = 450, R = 150, S = 900), which sheet allowed ALL light to pass through, behaving like a clear glass sheet?
options: Sheet S
Sheet P
Sheet Q
Sheet R
answer: Sheet S

question: A student measured shadow heights at different object-to-screen distances while keeping the torch position fixed: at 10 cm apart, shadow was 8 cm; at 20 cm apart, shadow was 12 cm; at 30 cm apart, shadow was 16 cm. What conclusion can be drawn from this data?
options: As distance between object and screen increases, shadow height increases
As distance between object and screen increases, shadow height decreases
Distance between object and screen does not affect shadow height
Moving the screen closer to the object makes the shadow taller
answer: As distance between object and screen increases, shadow height increases

question: An opaque cutout of the letter 'F' is placed between a light source and a screen. What shape will the shadow cast on the screen have?
options: The letter F shape
A plain square shape
A circular shape
No shadow will be cast
answer: The letter F shape
